meta.title: Web Request: Cache Miss Flow
meta.subtitle: Cache-Aside Pattern: Browser -> API -> Redis (Miss) -> PostgreSQL -> Cache Fill -> 200 OK

views.label: 1. Cache Miss
views.note: API checks Redis, resulting in a cache miss

views.label: 2. DB Fallback
views.note: API queries PostgreSQL for authoritative records

views.label: 3. Cache Fill & Response
views.note: API populates Redis with TTL and returns 200 OK

messages.label: nil (cache miss)
messages.note: Key not found or expired TTL

cards.title: 1. Client Request & Cache Check
items: Browser issues GET /api/data to the API Server
API performs an O(1) in-memory key lookup in Redis (GET cache:key)
Sub-millisecond lookup minimizes load on the relational database

cards.title: 2. Cache Miss Detection
items: Redis keyspace returns nil (key not found or TTL expired)
API intercepts miss and initiates primary database query fallback
Client remains on hold while downstream systems resolve

cards.title: 3. PostgreSQL Query & Fetch
items: API executes parameterized SELECT against PostgreSQL
PostgreSQL reads indexes/disk to retrieve authoritative rows
PostgreSQL streams result set back to the API connection pool

cards.title: 4. Cache Population & Return
items: API executes SETEX cache:key 3600 to fill cache with TTL
Redis confirms write with OK; future requests become instant hits
API formats JSON response and delivers 200 OK to the browser

cards.title: System Architecture & Trade-Offs
items: Pattern: Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading) keeps memory footprint lean and resilient
Cache Stampede: Guard hot expired keys via mutex locking or early probabilistic refresh
Resilience: If Redis is unavailable, API gracefully degrades to query PostgreSQL directly
